Maqsadim — NASA ochiq ma’lumotlari yordamida atmosferadagi ozon o‘zgarishlarini kuzatish, tahlil qilish va xaritada ko‘rsatadigan aqlli tizim yaratish. Texnologiya, kosmos, sun’iy yo‘ldoshlar va sun’iy intellektga qiziqaman. Hozir loyihaga dasturchi, ma’lumotlar tahlilchisi va ilmiy tadqiqotga qiziquvchi faol jamoa a’zolarini izlayapman. Birgalikda foydali va innovatsion loyiha yaratmoqchiman.
summary: O3-NET-1 is a phone-friendly tool that helps anyone see whether the ozone layer is recovering in their own region. It turns NASA OMI/Aura total-column ozone observations into a clear chart, a trend estimate with uncertainty, and a plain-language explanation. It has three steps: Explore (choose a place and years), Analyze (see the seasonal cycle and trend in Dobson Units), and Verify (see the data source, method and limits). It answers the four questions of the challenge: what is changing, where, how much, and whether the change is significant. In this prototype we used real NASA OMI data for Tashkent (January 2023 to November 2026, 890 daily values), and the tool estimates a trend together with its uncertainty. It matters because ozone recovery is slow and uneven, so people need clear evidence they can check.
details: WHAT IT DOES O3-NET-1 is a mobile-friendly web tool for exploring atmospheric ozone. A user picks a place and years, sees a chart of total-column ozone in Dobson Units (DU), gets a trend estimate with a 95% interval in plain language, and can check the data source, method and limits. It also includes a 7-step animated story that explains how the ozone layer works, what damaged it, how it is recovering, and why adding artificial ozone is not practical. HOW IT WORKS 1. Explore: choose a data source and a year range. Users can add their own CSV files from the NOAA GML OMI/OMPS time-series tool, which serves NASA OMI/Aura data. 2. Analyze: daily values are averaged into monthly means (at least 8 days per month). The yearly cycle is removed by subtracting the average of each calendar month. A straight line is fitted by least squares, and the 95% interval is widened when neighbouring months are correlated. A trend is shown only for 3 years or more. We call a change significant only when the 95% interval excludes zero (an approximate test). 3. Verify: the page lists the product, units, number of days with data, quality notes, the method, and the limitations. RESULTS SO FAR We retrieved real NASA OMI/Aura total-column ozone for Tashkent (41.3 N, 69.3 E) from January 2023 to 11 November 2026: 890 daily values, which became 46 monthly means. They show a clear seasonal cycle, with the highest values in winter and spring and the lowest in autumn. The estimated change after removing the seasons is -22 DU per decade, with a 95% interval of -98 to +55 DU. The interval includes zero, so the change is not statistically significant at the 95% level (approximate test). Yearly averages (315, 334 and 312 DU for 2023 to 2025) swing as much as the signal, so four years is too short to show a long-term trend. The tool says this in plain words instead of over-claiming. We cross-checked the app's result with an independent calculation (same numbers), and we tested the trend code on a clearly labelled test file where it recovered the trend built into it. The sample regions in the demo are made-up numbers and are labelled as such. BENEFITS AND GOALS Students, teachers and citizens can understand ozone recovery in their own region without special software. Our goal is a Eurasia network of places with 15 to 20 years of data each, with every number shown together with its source, units and uncertainty. LIMITS Total-column ozone is not the same as ozone pollution near the ground. The tool uses one 0.25 degree grid cell per place. The exact product version still has to be confirmed in NASA documentation. O3-NET-1 is an independent concept and prototype. It is not an official NASA project, not endorsed by NASA, and not a launched satellite. It is not a health warning or an ozone-hole detector. TOOLS HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript in a single file (no server, no libraries), SVG charts, Python for data checks, the NOAA GML time-series tool to retrieve NASA OMI data, and the AI assistant Claude (Anthropic) for drafting. Use of Super Intelligence (SI): select
